CPESR Exam 2 — Tagging Pilot

55 questions, transcribed + tagged from the image-based source, same format as Exam 1.

Q1. Line DE is prolonged to Point F by double centering. Length F'F" is 0.84 ft. Length DE and EF are 721.44 ft and 614.23 ft, respectively. What is the angular error introduced in a single plunging?
IIfieldProgram T — partial

  • A) 0°4'42"
  • B) 0°1'5"
  • C) 0°2'21"
  • D) 0°2'10"
F'F"/2 = 0.84/2 = 0.42 ft (average error, since two additional shots F' and F" exist); tanθ = 0.42/614.23 → θ = 0°2'21". A small-angle right-triangle solve — could use Program T's right-triangle branch, but the halving-for-average step first is manual.
Answer: C
Q2. Cross section areas from a plan (scale H:1"=40', V:1"=10') at sta 4+73 (5.43 in²) and sta 3+89 (7.82 in²). Determine the volume between the stations, rounded to the nearest hundred CY.
IIIarea


  • A) 8400 CY
  • B) 2100 CY
  • C) 8200 CY
  • D) 33000 CY

Plan scale to real world ground scale

1 in² = 40' × 10' = 400 ft²

Sta 4+73 Area = 5.43 in² × 400 ft²/in² = 2172 ft²

Sta 3+89 Area = 7.82 in² × 400 ft²/in² = 3128 ft²

Using average end area method to calculate volume

V = (A₁+A₂)/2 × L

V = (2172+3128)/2 × (473−389) = 222,600 ft³

222,600 ft³ × 1 yd³/27 ft³ = 8244.44 CY ≈ 8200 CY

Answer: C
Q3. Which of the following are true statements: (A) Random error can be present in all surveying measurements. (B) Random error can be either positive or negative. (C) Random errors are typically caused by factors beyond the surveyor's control. (D) Random errors can still remain after all mistakes and systemic errors have been eliminated.
Itheory
  • A) C, D
  • B) A, D
  • C) B, C
  • D) A, B, C, D
All four statements are true of random errors — they occur in all measurements, can be positive or negative, are outside the surveyor's control, and remain even after mistakes/systematic errors are removed.
Answer: D
Q4. An area of a parcel shown on a map is 8728 ft². If the map scale factor is 0.99756, what is the actual ground area?
IIIarea
  • A) 8749.35 ft²
  • B) 8706.70 ft²
  • C) 8685.46 ft²
  • D) 8770.75 ft²
Scale factor applies per linear dimension, so area needs the square: ground area = 8728/(0.99756)² = 8770.75 ft².
Answer: D
Q5. In a leveling field book, the correct procedure for checking the computed elevations is to
IIlevel
  • A) repeat all computations twice
  • B) average all backsights and foresight
  • C) subtract the sum of the foresights from the sum of the backsights and check to see if this number added to the start elevation equals the end elevation
  • D) add and subtract backsight and foresight starting from the last course to the first course
Subtracting the sum of foresights from the sum of backsights and checking that this, added to the start elevation, equals the end elevation is the correct procedure to ensure accuracy.
Answer: C
Q6. What is the purpose of plunging a surveying instrument?
IIfield
  • A) To increase the accuracy of a recorded measurement by averaging in another measurement on the same point while the instrument is in the inverted position.
  • B) To lower the instrument to the lowest possible height in order to take the BS and FS readings without adjusting the location.
  • C) To take the next measurement on the next point without a new setup point.
  • D) To increase the accuracy of a recorded measurement by providing another measurement to compare which is closest to the known point.
Plunging rotates the instrument 180° along both vertical and horizontal axes to take a second measurement on the same point; averaging that with the first reading increases accuracy and cancels out most instrument maladjustments.
Answer: A
Q7. A composite figure: base rectangle 300'×50', with a left triangular peak (100' base, slope 1:5 → 20' rise), a center notch (50' base, slope 1:1.25 → 20' drop), and a right triangular peak (150' base, slope 1:3 → 50' rise). What is the area of the figure?
IIIarea

  • A) 20250 yd²
  • B) 2222 yd²
  • C) 20000 yd²
  • D) 2250 yd²

Area of triangles: \(\dfrac{[(100\times 20)+(50\times 20)+(150\times 50)]}{2}\)= 5250 ft² Area of rectangle: 300×50 = 15,000 ft² Total Area: 5250 + 15,000 = 20,250 ft² 20,250 ÷ 9 = 2250 yd²

Answer: D
Q8. Given tangent bearings N44°42'4"E and S41°48'32"W at the two ends of a horizontal curve, what is the central angle θ?
Vhc

  • A) 89°24'8"
  • B) 86°48'32"
  • C) 87°6'28"
  • D) 83°37'4"

Tangent of the curve creates a 90° angle with the radius. Calculate the angle between the vertical line through the BVC and the radius (angle DCB): angle DCB = 180° − 44°42'4" − 90° = 45°17'56" Opposite angles of a line intersecting two parallel lines are equal: angle DCB = angle ABC Add angle ABC and angle ABE: Δ = 45°17'56" + 41°48'32" = 87°6'28"

Answer: C
Q9. A transit is set up over Point A, HI=4.72 ft. Elevation of A is 347.72 ft. Zenith angle to a target with rod reading 5.21 ft on Point B is 102°43'52". Slope distance between transit and target is 321.73 ft. What is the vertical difference between Point A and Point B?
IIstadia
  • A) −72.2
  • B) 70.9
  • C) −70.9
  • D) −71.39

4.72 − 5.21 − (321.73)sin(102°43'52" − 90°) = −71.39 ft

Answer: D
Q10. Curve radius R=25', line CD offset 11 ft to the north of the tangent through A, central angle 90°. What is the curve distance AB?
VhcProgram S — partial

  • A) 24.41 ft
  • B) 17.28 ft
  • C) 27.88 ft
  • D) 21.99 ft

(PT can only move parallel in the x-direction, so the tangent offset from point A is 25−11=14 ft): tangent offset = 25 − 11 = 14 ft 14 = R(1 − cos I) = 25(1 − cos I) I = 63°53'46" arc AB = 2πR × (\(\dfrac{63^{\circ}53'46"}{360^{\circ}}\)) = 2π(25) × (\(\dfrac{63^{\circ}53'46"}{360^{\circ}}\)) = 27.88 ft Program S note: Program S computes arc length once I=63°53'46" is known (enter R=25, Q?=63.5346 DMS, leave A?=0), but deriving I itself from the 14-ft external offset isn't part of S's normal cycle — manual step first.

Answer: C
Q11. A surveyor on a downward sloping hill measures 43.72 ft perpendicular-intended to a tree, but the tape sits 3.5 ft below the true perpendicular point on the tree. What is the true horizontal distance between the surveyor and the tree?
IIdist
  • A) 40.22 ft
  • B) 43.71 ft
  • C) 43.86 ft
  • D) 43.58 ft

HD = √(43.72² − 3.5²) = 43.58 ft

Answer: D
Q12. On a standard topographic map with scale 1:50,000, a ground distance of 21,625 ft would be represented by a map distance of
IVphoto
  • A) 5.19 inches
  • B) 7.12 inches
  • C) 0.43 inches
  • D) 0.19 inches
1/50,000 = x/(21,625×12 in/ft) → x = 5.19 inches (unitless ratio scale assumed as 1 in : 50,000 in when not otherwise stated).
Answer: A
Q13. Two cross sections of excavation (triangular shaded areas) at sta 236+78 (140' wide, 3.5:1 slope, offset 230 shown) and sta 238+96 (50' wide, height 72.15'). What is the total volume to be removed along this stretch?
IIIarea

  • A) 33498 cu yds
  • B) 25851 cu yds
  • C) 29685 cu yds
  • D) 31679 cu yds
Area at Sta 236+78: height =\(\dfrac{230}{3.5}\)= 65.71' area =\(\dfrac{(140\times 65.71)}{2}\)= 4599.7 ft² Area at Sta 238+96: area =\(\dfrac{(50\times 72.15)}{2}\)= 1803.75 ft² Total volume of excavation: V =\(\dfrac{L(A_{1}+A_{2})}{2}\)=\(\dfrac{(23896-23678)(4599.7+1803.75)}{2}\)= 697,976 ft³ = 25,851 yd³

Answer: B
Q14. You want to examine the terrain of a remote construction site. The survey you use is a
Iintro
  • A) route survey
  • B) topographic survey
  • C) boundary survey
  • D) land survey
A topographic survey determines locations of natural and artificial features and elevations — appropriate for examining terrain.
Answer: B
Q15. Which of the following instruments would be most useful for underground mapping?
IIfield
  • A) Total Station
  • B) Bathometer
  • C) Altimeter
  • D) Gyrotheodolite
A gyrotheodolite (gyroscope mounted to a theodolite) determines true north orientation without seeing the stars — used in mine surveying and tunnel engineering. An altimeter measures altitude (aircraft use); a bathometer measures water depth.
Answer: D
Q16. A sewer line extends to a new MH2 (proposed invert 114.22), pipe laid flat along excavated ground. Existing ground slope MH1 to MH2 is 2.2%. If MH2's invert is lowered 1.4 ft, the excavated slope becomes 3%. What is the excavated slope if the invert is lowered only 0.8 ft?
Vvc

  • A) 1.71%
  • B) 2.52%
  • C) 2.66%
  • D) 1.74%

Two equations (rise/run = slope), since pipe laid flat means pipe slope = excavation slope: \(\dfrac{(y+1.4)}{x}\)= 0.03 \(\dfrac{y}{x}\)= 0.022 → y = 0.022x Substituting: 0.022x+1.4 = 0.03x → x=175 ft, y=3.85 ft Slope if invert lowered 0.8 feet: \(\dfrac{(3.85+0.8)}{175}\)= 0.02657 = 2.66%

Answer: C
Q17. A road is built on the edge of a township. PC-side tangent bearing N6°12'9"W at N2587.18, E10333.57; PT-side tangent bearing N84°15'13"E at N1999.88, E10803.87. What radius is needed to complete the road?
VhcProgram S — partial

  • A) 752.40'
  • B) 484.25'
  • C) 481.43'
  • D) 534.16'

Find I using the tangent bearings given: 6°12'9" + 84°15'13" = 90°27'22" I = 180° − 90°27'22" = 89°32'38" Find the chord length using the coordinates given: Chord = √[(10803.87−10333.57)²+(1999.88−2587.18)²] = 752.40 ft Solve R using the chord equation: C = 2R·sin(\(\dfrac{I}{2}\)) → 752.40 = 2R·sin(\(\dfrac{89^{\circ}32'38"}{2}\)) → R = 534.16' Program S note: Chord input (C=752.40, Q?=89.3238 DMS, R?=0) solves this directly once I and chord are known — deriving both from bearings/coordinates is manual.

Answer: D
Q18. The initial point of NAD 27 is
IVspc
  • A) Topeka, Kansas
  • B) Cloverfield, Indiana
  • C) Meades Ranch, Kansas
  • D) Manhattan, Kansas
NAD 27's initial point is Meades Ranch, Kansas.
Answer: C
Q19. A dirt parkway is converted to a 4' sidewalk. Original ground (OG) and finish grade (FG) elevations are given below. Starting at 1+27, FG elevation = 756.94 with proposed slope −1.75%. What is the catch point station?
Vvc
StationOG Elev (ft)
1+27758.34
2+03757.58
3+00753.41
3+86751.23

  • A) 2+17.89
  • B) 2+92.14
  • C) 2+49.80
  • D) 2+80.39

Calculate the FG at each station: 756.94 − (203−127)(0.0175) = 755.61 756.94 − (300−127)(0.0175) = 753.91 756.94 − (386−127)(0.0175) = 752.41 By observation, the catch point is between 2+03 and 3+00. The OG slope is NOT constant across all stations, so use the actual OG slope in that specific stretch: Slope OG (2+03 to 3+00) =\(\dfrac{(753.41-757.58)}{(300-203)}\)= −\(\dfrac{0.043 ft}{ft}\) Create two equations for the slope of OG and FG (using 3+00 as x for each). Original (existing) grade slope equation: OG: 753.41 = −0.043(300) + b → b = 766.31 → y = −0.043x + 766.31 Finish grade slope equation: FG: 753.91 = −0.0175(300) + b → b = 759.16 → y = −0.0175x + 759.16 Set both equations equal to each other: −0.0175(x) + 759.16 = −0.043(x) + 766.31 → x = 280.39 Catch point station = 2+80.39

Answer: D
Q20. A leveling run from BM2 (elev 1098.51) to MH#2 (elev 1094.05) has BS/FS readings at intermediate turning points, with the BS at sta 2+01 unknown. What is the BS of sta 2+01?
IIlevel
PointBSFSElev.Location
BM23.57(1098.51)
Sta 1+174.385.17top of pavement
TP13.132.79
Sta 2+01?4.71top of pavement
TP22.715.01
Sta 3+174.013.63top of pavement
MH #14.28manhole cover #1
MH #24.681094.05manhole cover #2

  • A) 3.73
  • B) 4.13
  • C) 2.15
  • D) 8.01
Find the elevation of TP2 and sta 2+01. From there solve for BS for sta 2+01. Elevation at sta 2+01: 1098.51 + 3.57 − 5.17 + 4.38 − 2.79 + 3.13 − 4.71 = 1096.92 Elevation at TP2: 1094.05 + 4.68 − 4.01 + 3.63 − 2.71 = 1095.64 BS at 2+01: 1096.92 + BS − 5.01 = 1095.64 BS = 3.73 Note: Typically if there is no BS in the BS box and it is not missing information, then it is a side shot. Therefore we omit MH#1 from the calculation.
Alternate method (from a student comment, confirmed correct by the instructor): find the elevation at Sta 3+17 using the final BM2→MH#2 closure, then set up sum(BS) + x − sum(FS) = required closure and solve directly for x. Multiple algebraically equivalent paths reach BS = 3.73.

Answer: A
Q21. In a mass diagram, the mass ordinate is the
Varea
  • A) the x and y coordinate at a particular point on the mass diagram
  • B) the sum of the volumes of cut and fill up to that point on the mass curve
  • C) the point of conversion from total cut to total fill
  • D) the cumulative volume of excavation and embankment for the entire project
Mass ordinates are the individual points making up the mass curve, representing cumulative excavation/embankment volume up to that station — there are infinitely many along the curve.
Answer: B
Q22. A Civil Engineer registered pre-1982 may do which of the following?
Ipls
  • A) Prepare a legal description
  • B) all of these
  • C) Prepare a parcel map
  • D) Lay out a shopping plaza using ALTA
A civil engineer registered before January 1, 1982 can perform the same operations as a registered land surveyor.
Answer: B
Q23. On a plan and profile sheet, the vertical scale of a proposed pipeline is 1/60. Ground horizontal distance between MH1 and MH2 is 79.4'. Vertical exaggeration is 6:1. What is this horizontal distance on the plan and profile sheet?
IVphoto
  • A) 7.94"
  • B) 2.65"
  • C) 13.23"
  • D) 15.88"
Vertical scale: 1/60 → 1"=5'. Horizontal scale from 6:1 exaggeration: (1/5)/(1/x)=6/1 → x=30, so 1"=30'. Plan distance = 79.4/30 = 2.65".
Answer: B
Q24. Which of the following is another way to characterize attribute data as the term is used in GIS?
IVgis
  • A) feature class data
  • B) spatial data
  • C) key
  • D) aspatial data
Attributes are characteristics of a spatial feature, usually stored in tabular format and linked by keys — attributes are aspatial (non-spatial) data.
Answer: D
Q25. The terms "metes and bounds" in a legal description describes
Ipls
  • A) boundary area
  • B) boundary elevations on the corners
  • C) coordinates of boundaries
  • D) bearings and lengths of the boundaries
"Metes and bounds" refers to the bearings and lengths (metes) and boundary/monument calls (bounds) describing a parcel.
Answer: D
Q26. A storm drain pipe runs from Point A (50 ft left of sta 3+50) to Point B (50 ft right of sta 5+00). Centerline radius is 600 ft. What is the length of the storm drain pipe?
VhcProgram T — partial

  • A) 179.50 feet
  • B) 163.55 feet
  • C) 600 feet
  • D) 151.70 feet

Construct a triangle using A, B, and the radius point (C) to the 600 ft radius curve. Since points A and B are radial to the centerline, angle ACB is the central angle of the horizontal curve from sta 3+50 to sta 5+00. Central angle I: I =\(\dfrac{L(360^{\circ})}{(R·2π)}\)=\(\dfrac{(150)(360^{\circ})}{(600·2π)}\)= 14.324° Use Law of Cosines to solve for length AB (radial distances CA = 650 ft, CB = 550 ft): c = √(a² + b² − 2ab·cos C) c = √(550² + 650² − 2(550)(650)cos 14.324°) c = √32,227.44 ft² = 179.52 ft Note: Program T's 2-sides+included-angle branch solves this directly once radial distances and I are known.

Answer: A
Q27. The latitude and departure of a traverse course with length 375.49 ft and bearing S39°17'00"W is
IIItravProgram A — partial
  • A) −290.64 ft, −237.74 ft
  • B) −250.64 ft, −279.59 ft
  • C) −237.74 ft, −290.64 ft
  • D) −279.59 ft, −250.64 ft

Draw the approximate location on a coordinate system (bearing S39°17'W, not to scale). \(\sin 39°17' = \dfrac{x}{375.49} \rightarrow x = 237.74 \text{ ft}\) \(\cos 39°17' = \dfrac{y}{375.49} \rightarrow y = 290.64 \text{ ft}\) Both negative since it is in quadrant III (SW): latitude = −290.64 ft, departure = −237.74 ft Note: Exactly one iteration of Program A's per-side loop.

Answer: A
Q28. An aerial photography project targets a 4.6×9.0 mile area (Porter Ranch). Photo scale 1:12,000, format 9"×9", end lap 60%, side lap 30%, focal length 6". Assuming N-S flight lines, what is the minimum number of flight lines required?
IVphoto

  • A) 2
  • B) 1
  • C) 3
  • D) 4
Find ground length: Ground length = (Format Size) × (\(\dfrac{1}{Photo Scale}\)) = 9 in × \(\dfrac{12,000}{12}\) = 9,000 ft Find max distance between flight lines: FL_MaxDist = (Ground Length) × (1 − Side Lap) = 9,000 ft × (1 − 0.30) = 6,300 ft Minimum number of flight lines: FL_Min# = \(\dfrac{(Target Area Width)}{FL_{\text{MaxDist}}}\) = (4.6 miles × 5,280 ft/mile) / 6,300 ft = 3.86 Rounding up = 4

Answer: D
Q29. Sanitary sewer line 2 (SS2) must have min 2 ft clearance below SS1 crossing at MH2, with +1.1% slope from MH4 to MH5. SS1 (9" OD HDPE) runs MH1 (sta 7+89, EL 86.98) to MH3 (sta 10+12, EL 83.75), slope crosses at sta 8+96. SS2 (6" ID HDPE) crosses at sta 8+21, wall thickness 0.5" both pipes, elevations at top of pipe. MH4 at sta 6+41. What is the highest possible invert elevation at MH4?
Vconstr

  • A) 79.91'
  • B) 80.20'
  • C) 79.34'
  • D) 80.16'

Elevation of SS1 at Sta 8+96: Slope of pipe =\(\dfrac{(83.75 - 86.98)}{(1012 - 789)}\)= −0.0145 Length from MH1 to MH2 = 896 − 789 = 107 ft Elevation change = 107(−0.0145) = −1.55 Elev SS1 at MH2 = 86.98 − 1.55 = 85.43 = top of SS1 pipe Invert elevation of SS2 at Sta 8+21 (Note: Station 8+96 on SS1 is at the same location as Sta 8+21 on SS2): Invert(Sta 8+21) = 85.43 −\(\dfrac{9}{12}\)− 2 −\(\dfrac{0.5}{12}\)−\(\dfrac{6}{12}\)= 82.14' Invert elevation at Sta 6+41 (MH4) (Note: The arrow of a slope usually points downhill unless there is a sign in front of the number. If that is the case, the arrow points in whatever direction the sign is in. In this case, the +1.1% points towards MH5 so it is an upwards slope towards MH5. If there is no sign in front of the slope, the arrow points downhill.): Distance MH2–MH4 = 821 − 641 = 180 ft Invert(Sta 6+41) = 82.14 − 180(0.011) = 80.16 ft

Answer: D
Q30. Line AB is measured to be 78.34' ± 0.007'. Line CD is measured to be 89.11' ± 0.012'. What is the sum of these two lines?
IIItheory
  • A) 167.45' ± 0.000'
  • B) 167.45' ± 0.019'
  • C) 167.45' ± 0.005'
  • D) 167.45' ± 0.014'
Error of sum = √(0.007²+0.012²) = 0.014; sum = 78.34+89.11 = 167.45' ± 0.014'.
Answer: D
Q31. An aerial photograph was taken at a height of 11,500 ft above the terrain with a 6 in focal length camera, using a standard 9"×9" format. What is most nearly the acreage in this photograph?
IVphoto
  • A) 5,467 acres
  • B) 3,434 acres
  • C) 1,144 acres
  • D) 6,831 acres
Photo scale = f/H = 6/11,500 → 1in=1,916.67 ft; ground length = 9×1,916.67 = 17,250 ft; area = 17,250²/43,560 = 6,831.1 acres.
Answer: D
Q32. The radius of the centerline of a highway curve is 2200 ft and the deflection angle to point B on the curve is 4°17'. What is the length of the highway from A to B, most nearly?
VhcProgram S — partial

  • A) 328.94
  • B) 330.14
  • C) 164.47
  • D) 273.27
Deflection angle is half the central angle: \(\dfrac{I}{2}\)= 4°17' I = 8°34' Arc length: L =\(\dfrac{2π(R)(I)}{360}\) L = 328.94 ft Note: Program S computes arc length directly once the true central angle Δ (not the deflection angle) is known — doubling the given deflection angle first is a manual step.

Answer: A
Q33. The City has approved a man-made recreational lake inside a 30 acre park. What type of survey is needed before construction?
Iintro
  • A) As-built survey
  • B) Topographic survey
  • C) GPS survey
  • D) Hydrological survey
As-built surveys are for after construction; hydrological survey is for existing bodies of water (this lake doesn't exist yet); GPS is an instrument/method, not a survey type. A topographic survey determines current elevations, which is what's needed before design.
Answer: B
Q34. The survey crew sights two identical Philadelphia rods (Rod-A and Rod-B) through an instrument's crosshairs (illustrated reticle views). What are the center hair readings on each rod? Which rod is at a higher elevation? Which is closer to the instrument?
IIstadia

  • A) Rod-A center hair reading: 7.42
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.26
    Rod-A is located at a higher elevation than Rod-B
    Rod-A is located closer to the instrument
  • B) Rod-A center hair reading: 3.74
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.54
    Rod-B is located at a higher elevation than Rod-A
    Rod-B is located closer to the instrument
  • C) Rod-A center hair reading: 7.42
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.26
    Rod-B is located at a higher elevation than is Rod-A
    Rod-A is located closer to the instrument
  • D) Rod-A center hair reading: 7.26
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.42
    Rod-B is located at a higher elevation to the instrument than Rod-A
    Rod-A is located closer to the instrument
Read the center hair (middle crosshair) off each rod's reticle view: Rod-A center hair reading = 7.42 Rod-B center hair reading = 7.26 Compare elevations: A lower rod reading means the ground under that rod is higher (same line of sight from the instrument). Rod-B reads lower (7.26 < 7.42), so Rod-B is at the higher elevation. Compare distance to instrument: The rod whose graduations appear larger in the reticle view is the rod that is closer to the instrument (less distance = larger apparent stadia image). Rod-A's markings appear larger, so Rod-A is closer to the instrument.

Answer: C
Q35. The magnetic declination of line PQ is 6°17'56"E with a magnetic bearing of N23°22'14"W. If 50 years ago the declination was 1°13'12"W, what was the magnetic bearing 50 years ago?
IIIang
  • A) N15°51'6"W
  • B) N26°2'46"W
  • C) N18°17'30"W
  • D) N17°4'18"W

True bearing never changes: the line does not move on the coordinate plane. The declination changes which changes the magnetic bearing reading, but the true line never moves. The magnetic bearing is measured from the magnetic declination line as if the declination were the true north line. 23°22'14" − 6°17'56" = 17°4'18" N17°4'18"W = true bearing 17°4'18" − 1°13'12" = 15°51'6" N15°51'6"W = magnetic bearing 50 years ago

Answer: A
Q36. Geology determined that the material between 4 feet and 11 feet contains Type C soil which is not sufficient for the project. It will need to be removed and replaced with competent material. What is the approximate volume of earth between depth 4 and 11 feet?
IIIarea
Depth(ft)Area(ft²)
2 ft435
3 ft485
4 ft520
6 ft740
9 ft1120
10 ft1200
11 ft1285
14 ft1610
  • A) 1580 CY
  • B) 240 CY
  • C) 1745 ft³
  • D) 65 CY
Average end area method, applied between each successive pair of given depths from 4 ft to 11 ft: V = L(\(\dfrac{(A_{1} + A_{2})}{2}\)) V₄₋₁₁ =\(\dfrac{2(520+740)}{2}\)+\(\dfrac{3(740+1120)}{2}\)+\(\dfrac{1(1120+1200)}{2}\)+\(\dfrac{1(1200+1285)}{2}\) V₄₋₁₁ = 1260 + 2790 + 1160 + 1242.5 V₄₋₁₁ = 6452.5 ft³ = 240 CY

Answer: B
Q37. Point E=(1000,1000), Point D=(900,1600). Bearing CE=N78°14'29"E, distance CE=167.49 ft. What is the bearing of CD?
IIItrav

  • A) N11°31'15"E
  • B) S5°45'38"W
  • C) S84°14'22"W
  • D) N5°45'38"E

Find the complement of the bearing angle CE: 90° − 78°14'29" = 11°45'31" Solve for the local x,y offsets of point C relative to E: \(\sin 11°45'31" = \dfrac{y}{167.49} \rightarrow y = 34.13 \text{ ft}\) \(\cos 11°45'31" = \dfrac{x}{167.49} \rightarrow x = 163.98 \text{ ft}\) Coordinates of C: C(x,y) = (1000 − 163.98, 1000 − 34.13) = (836.03, 965.87) Bearing angle of CD: tan θ =\(\dfrac{(900 - 836.03)}{(1600 - 965.87)}\) θ = 5°45'38" = N5°45'38"E

Answer: D
Q38. On a map, two contour lines are 1.5 cm apart, contour interval 1 meter. Map scale is 1:2000. What is the slope between these two contours?
IVtopo
  • A) 1.50%
  • B) 0.15%
  • C) 5.00%
  • D) 3.33%
Ground distance = 1.5cm×2000 = 3000cm = 30 m; slope = 1/30 = 3.33%.
Answer: D
Q39. A road profile has BVC at sta 5+00 (elev 250.00 ft, grade +5.5%), PVI at sta 17+00 (elev 316.00 ft), and EVC at sta 29+00 (elev 358.00 ft, grade +3.5%). The typical road cross section has a 22 ft travel way at 2% sloping down from centerline, then a 6" curb, then a 10 ft area at 2% sloping down to the toe of slope. What is the elevation of the toe of slope at sta 19+50?
VvcProgram P — partial

  • A) 320.79 ft
  • B) 321.03 ft
  • C) 320.89 ft
  • D) 321.25 ft
Curve is symmetric: PVI sta 17+00 is the midpoint of BVC (5+00) and EVC (29+00), so total curve length L = 24 stations (2400 ft). Elevation on the vertical curve at sta 19+50 (x = 19+50 − 5+00 = 14.5 stations from BVC): elev = elev_BVC + g1·x + (\(\dfrac{(g2-g1)}{(2L)}\))·x² elev = 250.00 + 5.5(14.5) + (\(\dfrac{(3.5-5.5)}{(2·24)}\))(14.5)² elev = 250.00 + 79.75 − 8.76 = 320.99 ft (centerline profile grade) Cross slope down to the toe of slope (22 ft at 2% to the curb, plus 10 ft at 2% beyond the 6" curb): toe elev = 320.99 − (22×0.02) + 0.5 + (10×0.02) toe elev = 320.99 − 0.44 + 0.5 + 0.20 = 321.25 ft

Answer: D
Q40. The radius of the arc is 750 ft; tangent bearing N88°15'18"E, radius bearing at EC S41°48'32"W. What is the area of the shaded segment (between chord BC-EC and the arc)?
Vhc

  • A) 9.82 acres
  • B) 12.90 acres
  • C) 6.45 acres
  • D) 3.37 acres
Segment area = sector area − triangle area, using the central angle Δ derived from the given tangent/radius bearings. Source solution's worked steps were mostly outside the captured screenshot area (only the tail-end comments were visible) — answer confirmed from the marked correct choice.
Answer: D
Q41. If 90 percent of all contours on a map must be within 2.5 feet error, what contour interval is necessary?
IVtopo
  • A) 1.25 ft
  • B) 2.5 ft
  • C) 10 ft
  • D) 5 ft
Per National Map Accuracy standards, no more than 10% of elevations may be in error of more than 1/2 contour interval. If 90% must be within 2.5 ft, that 2.5 ft equals 1/2 the contour interval, so the full interval = 5 ft.
Answer: D
Q42. A vertical curve L=1800 ft, G1=−1.4%, G2=+3.7%, EVC at sta 75+27, elev 157.61 ft. What is the elevation at sta 71+33?
VvcProgram P — full

  • A) 145.23 ft
  • B) 129.87 ft
  • C) 165.93 ft
  • D) 173.24 ft
Find elevation of the PVI, working back from EVC: elev_EVC = elev_PVI + g2(\(\dfrac{L}{2}\)) 157.62 = elev_PVI + 3.7(\(\dfrac{18}{2}\)) elev_PVI = 124.31 ft Find elevation of BVC: elev_BVC = elev_PVI − g1(\(\dfrac{L}{2}\)) elev_BVC = 124.31 + 1.4(\(\dfrac{18}{2}\)) elev_BVC = 136.91 ft Station of BVC: sta BVC = 75+27 − 1800 = 57+27 Elevation on the curve at sta 71+33 (x = distance from BVC, in stations): elev_x =\(\dfrac{(R·x^{2})}{2}\)+ g1·x + elev_BVC x = 7133 − 5727 = 1406 ft = 14+06 elev_x = (\(\dfrac{(3.7+1.4)}{18}\))(14.06²)/2 − 1.4(14.06) + 136.91 elev_x = 145.23 ft

Answer: A
Q43. A sewer line curve connects two manholes, radius 100'. EC of the curve is the center of MH#1; tangent at MH#1 is parallel to the centerline. MH#2 is at 15' Rt of centerline sta 33+65. MH#1 is at 8' Lt of centerline. What is the road centerline stationing for MH#1?
Vconstr

  • A) sta 33+07
  • B) sta 33+05
  • C) sta 33+01
  • D) sta 33+04

The vertical distance from the radius point down to the line through MH1/MH2 is 77 ft (from the 15' and 8' offsets and the geometry shown). Solve for the horizontal offset X: X = √(100² − 77²) = 63.80 ft Station at EC (MH1): Station at EC MH1 = 33.65 − 0.6380 = 33.0120 = 33+01.2 Note: Rt of centerline and Lt of centerline mean right and left of the centerline. The direction of right or left is determined by direction of increasing stationing. Anything left of an increasing stationing is considered left of centerline and anything right of an increasing stationing is considered right of centerline.

Answer: C
Q44. All of the following is information shown on a lath except
Vconstr
  • A) Offset
  • B) Angle to the next stake
  • C) Cut or fill
  • D) Elevation
Angle to the next stake is not shown on a lath — laths typically show offset, cut/fill, and elevation/station info, not angular data to adjacent stakes.
Answer: B
Q45. [Same field notes as Exam1 Q3] Assuming a uniform grade between recorded cross section points, the ground elevation at a point 24 ft left of centerline at sta 6+00 is
IIIlevel

  • A) 109.17 ft
  • B) 110.47 ft
  • C) 109.95 ft
  • D) 112.87 ft
Interpolate FS between 20L(6.10) and 30L(7.40): rate=(7.4−6.1)/10=0.13/ft; FS at 24L=6.10+0.13(4)=6.62; elevation = 111.73+4.30−4.48+3.87−4.12+5.27−6.62 = 109.95 ft.
Answer: C
Q46. This active remote sensing technique in LiDAR is similar to radar but uses
IIlidar
  • A) laser light pulses
  • B) direct photos
  • C) radio waves
  • D) GPS
LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) is an active remote sensing technique analogous to radar, but instead of radio waves it emits pulses of laser light and measures the time/phase of the return to determine distance.

Answer: A
Q47. Dashed line = existing ground, solid lines = new road section, with elevation/offset pairs at 7 points forming a cross section. If constant between sta 15+00 and 16+00, what is the quantity of earthwork?
IIIarea

  • A) 735 yd³ cut
  • B) 1470 yd³ cut
  • C) 593 yd³ fill
  • D) 1143 yd³ fill
The top number represents the elevation at that point. The bottom number represents the distance from the centerline. Use the Coordinate Method: pick a point and proceed clockwise. 0(56−56) = 0 −15(54−57) = 45 −17(63.5−56) = −127.5 −20(61.5−54) = −150 0(59.5−63.5) = 0 20(54−61.5) = −150 17(56−59.5) = −59.5 15(57−54) = 45 Σ = −397 Cross sectional area: cross sectional area = −\(\dfrac{397}{2}\)= |−198.5| = 198.5 ft² Multiply by length of road section: \(\dfrac{198.5(100)}{27}\)= 735 yd³ cut

Answer: A
Q48. A road must be detoured around a store with an offset of 40' (20' per S-curve reversal), radius remains 2000 ft for each equal curve. How much longer is the road between A and B than before the offset (straight D distance)?
VhcProgram S — partial

  • A) 5.35 ft
  • B) 0.95 ft
  • C) 10.70 ft
  • D) 3.76 ft

Tangent offset: Tangent offset = R(1 − cos I) 20 = 2000(1 − cos I) I = 8°6'35" Straight-line (x) distance for one arc: x distance for one arc = R sin I = 282.14 ft D = 282.14 × 4 = 1128.56 ft Arc distance for one arc: arc distance for one arc = 2πR × (\(\dfrac{8^{\circ}6'35"}{360^{\circ}}\)) arc distance for one arc = 283.08 ft total arc distance = 283.08 × 4 = 1132.32 ft Difference: Difference = 1132.32 − 1128.56 = 3.76 ft

Answer: D
Q49. What feature does the illustrated contour display, and in what quadrant would you expect the slope to be largest?
IVtopo

  • A) stream, SW
  • B) ridge, NE
  • C) stream, NE
  • D) ridge, SW
The pointy parts of the contours point toward larger contour values (uphill), which is the signature of a stream (a ridge would point the opposite way, toward smaller values). Contour lines packed closest together — here toward the SW/70 end — signify the steepest slope.
Answer: A

Q51. You're a project engineer early in pre-design for a major two-block development. A site layout has been prepared; a parking lot is the first stage. You need to identify possible overhead utilities. What should you do?
Iintro
  • A) Conduct a field investigation
  • B) Call USA
  • C) Contact the contractor
  • D) Mark plans for potholing
A field investigation locates where overhead/underground utilities may exist. USA/Dig Alert is called closer to construction to locate lines. Potholing measures depth of underground utilities (not overhead). The contractor likely isn't hired yet at this early stage.
Answer: A
Q52. Which of the following will not affect the use of an EDM?
IIfield
  • A) Buildings in the area
  • B) Light wave interference
  • C) Asphalt interference
  • D) Radiowave interference
Physical barriers (buildings) affect accuracy; EDMs rely on either light-wave velocity or high-frequency radio waves, so interference with either affects accuracy. Asphalt does not directly affect EDM accuracy.
Answer: C
Q53. What is the correct order for the use of surveys and staking for an engineering project?
Iintro
  • A) Boundary, Control, As-built, Construction Staking
  • B) Control, Boundary, Construction Staking, As-built
  • C) Construction Staking, Boundary, Control, As-built
  • D) As-built, Construction Staking, Control, Boundary
A project starts with a control survey (basepoints), then a boundary survey to identify limits of work, then construction staking to mark specific locations, and finally an as-built survey to record final elevations once work is complete.
Answer: B

Q55. The centerline of a road has a length of 1000 feet as shown (sag vertical curve, PVI sta 16+23, elev 342.76, G1=−2.5%, G2=+4.6%, L=10 sta). If a storm floods this road and reaches an elevation of 360 feet, what length of the vertical curve would be under water?
VvcProgram P — partial

  • A) 900 feet
  • B) 860 feet
  • C) 1000 feet
  • D) 930 feet
Find elevations at BVC and EVC (L/2 = 5 sta each side of PVI): elev BVC = 342.76 + 2.5(5) = 355.26 ft (below 360) elev EVC = 342.76 + 4.6(5) = 365.76 ft (above 360) Since BVC is below flood elevation and EVC is above it, the curve is underwater from BVC through the low point and up to where it crosses elevation 360 on the EVC side. Solve for x (distance from BVC, in stations) where the curve elevation equals 360: elev(x) = elev_BVC + G1·x + (\(\dfrac{(G2-G1)}{(2L)}\))·x² 360 = 355.26 − 2.5x + (\(\dfrac{(4.6-(-2.5))}{(2·10)}\))x² 0.355x² − 2.5x − 4.74 = 0 x = 8.596 sta (positive root within 0–10 sta) Length underwater: x = 8.596 sta = 859.6 ft ≈ 860 ft

Answer: B
